mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry, passport office, or other competent authority in the country of origin of the UBO or director

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner and director, such as a utility bill or recent bank statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility provider or licensed financial institution, then certified by a licensed notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, articles of association, register of members, and register of directors of any corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or company registrar in the corporate UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the origin jurisdiction is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate or certificate of good conduct for each ultimate beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police authority, criminal records bureau, or equivalent competent authority in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of wealth summary for each ultimate beneficial owner identified as a PEP or high-net-worth customer in a high-risk jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed regulated financial institution where the UBO maintains an account, countersigned by a licensed notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if required by the origin jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, and known counterparties against the United Nations Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, HM Treasury Consolidated List of Financial Sanctions Targets, and all Vanuatu domestic sanctions and public notices issued by VFSC and the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit. Each person must also be screened against a reputable international PEP database; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, family members, close associates, and all persons connected to FATF high-risk jurisdictions. Source of funds and source of wealth must be documented for any PEP or high-risk relationship before incorporation. Senior management approval is required before accepting a PEP or sanction-adjacent relationship. Continuous sanctions monitoring is required from filing day through the whole corporate life cycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: VFSC Company Registry - Vanuatu Financial Services Commission online company registration and name reservation portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered international company names must be expressed in Latin script. Official languages for company naming include English and French; Bislama is not a statutory registration script. If the intended corporate name originates from a non-Latin script, a certified transliteration in Latin characters is required, and the foreign-script form may not appear as the registered legal name. Names must be distinctive, not misleading, and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in the VFSC registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fund / Mutual Fund / Collective Investment Scheme
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension of the 30-day reservation window is available; if incorporation is not completed within the validity window, a fresh name reservation and fee are required. If the VFSC rejects a proposed name, the applicant may, within 14 days of receiving the written rejection notice, request written reasons from the Registrar. Within 21 days of receipt of those reasons, the applicant may file a formal appeal with the VFSC Appeals Tribunal together with a supporting legal opinion and any preliminary approvals from the relevant minister for restricted words. If the appeal is unsuccessful, judicial review may be filed in the Supreme Court of Vanuatu. In parallel, the applicant may submit an amended name through the online portal; doing so starts a new reservation period and requires a new name renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only if supplied by a VFSC-licensed international company registered agent and meeting the statutory requirement of a physical registered office in Vanuatu capable of receiving service of process. A standalone virtual office, P.O. Box, or non-Vanuatu address is not acceptable. The VFSC-licensed agent's physical premises may be used as the registered office address; however, for an ISIC 4649 pharmaceutical API wholesale operation, the licensed agent's virtual office does not constitute commercial substance and cannot be used for warehousing, distribution, or physical pharmaceutical activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated unannounced inspection risk due to the high-risk pharmaceutical API wholesale classification and AML/CFT sensitivity. The quantified risk of a VFSC or Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit unannounced on-site inspection is approximately 35-45% during the first 18 months of operation. The risk rises above 60% if any UBO is a PEP, if sanction-adjacent jurisdictions are involved, or if the company's transaction pattern triggers enhanced regulatory monitoring.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act No. 32 of 1992 [Cap 222], as amended, ss.3–8 (registration and incorporation); Business Licence Act [Cap 218], s.4 (mandatory business licensing); Pharmacy Act [Cap 32], as amended (pharmaceutical wholesale control).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Division, Port Vila, Efate, Republic of Vanuatu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of an International Company (VFSC Form IC-1) together with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and Consent to Act of directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed under the International Companies Act [Cap 222]; authorised capital is fixed in the Memorandum and Articles of Association (standard VUV 100,000 or equivalent in any permissible currency). No escrow, deposit-account, or capital-verification requirement applies at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the executed subscription statements are accepted and the initial share capital be allotted to the subscribers of record as determined by the directors; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at the office of its licensed registered agent in Port Vila, Efate, Vanuatu, and such agent is retained to keep the statutory register and corporate seal; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the natural persons named in the instrument of appointment are hereby appointed as first directors of the Company, and that a company secretary is appointed to maintain statutory books; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, to execute banking resolutions, and sign agreements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) via a licensed Vanuatu registered agent; correspondence filed with VFSC Companies Registry, Port Vila.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-availability request to the VFSC through the appointed licensed registered agent, confirming the proposed company name ('[Company Name] Ltd') does not conflict with registered domestic or international companies. Instruct the agent to execute the agent engagement letter and certify the registered-office arrangement in Port Vila before filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and three alternates
Statement of intended business scope (pharmaceutical API wholesale/distribution)
Passport copies of ultimate shareholders and beneficial owners
Declaration of non-resident ownership eligibility
Engagement letter with licensed VFSC registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is reserved by another entity or judged undesirable, VFSC will issue a query within one business day; the registered agent re-submits with the first alternate name and pays no additional search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment of Incorporation Application with VFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Companies Registry Division, Port Vila (dedicated International Companies filing desk).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Through the registered agent, file VFSC Form IC-1 with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, subscriber statements, and declarations of compliance. The application must designate the registered office, registered agent, initial directors, secretary, and share structure; statutory signatures must be witnessed by a notary public or the licensed agent.
required_dossiers: VFSC Form IC-1 (signed and witnessed)
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to Act of each director
Consent of registered agent and confirmation of registered office
Subscriber declaration and share allotment schedule
AML/KYC documentation for each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried on technical defects (e.g., missing witness signature or invalid share clause), VFSC issues a written requisition; the registered agent files corrective documents within 14 days, and the original five-business-day SLA restarts upon complete resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Government Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Finance and Administration Unit (cashier) or online payment portal; certification issued by Registrar of International Companies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the prescribed government registration fee and first-year company registry maintenance fee via bank transfer or VFSC portal, referencing the company file number. Upon confirmation of cleared funds, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under seal, which constitutes conclusive evidence of incorporation as an International Company.
required_dossiers: VFSC invoice and proof of wire payment
Company file number allocated at lodgment
Registered agent corporate account reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is not matched to the file due to missing wire reference, the agent submits a payment remittance advice to VFSC Finance; the certificate issues within one day of reconciliation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (statutory records) and the licensed registered agent (board book and share register administration).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or adopt written unanimous resolution) to allot shares, issue share certificates, approve the corporate seal, open the statutory registers, and ratify the registered office and agent appointments. File any director/secretary appointment notices with VFSC and maintain minutes and the register of members at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written resolutions of the first board meeting
Signed share certificates
Register of members, directors, and secretary
Corporate seal specimen and usage policy
Registered office and agent acceptance confirmations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC records show a mismatch between appointed and filed directors, the company secretary files a corrective notice with supporting board resolution; no late fee is applied if cured within the SLA window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Licence and Pharmaceutical Sector Licensing Coordination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Licence Registrar, Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), Port Vila; Department of Health, Ministry of Health (Pharmacy Unit) for pharmaceutical endorsement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Business Licence application under the Business Licence Act [Cap 218] describing the activity as 'wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and pharmaceutical raw materials'. Concurrently apply to the Department of Health for the pharmaceutical wholesale/import endorsement and, where required, a VFSC high-risk special-license assessment given the AML classification of the API trade. Upon approval, affix the licence at the registered office and display a certified copy at the physical warehouse.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (certified true copy)
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Business Licence application Form with activity code ISIC 4649
Pharmaceutical wholesale/import permit application to Department of Health
Site compliance report for temperature-controlled API storage
AML compliance manual and designated compliance officer statement
Fire safety certificate for licensed premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Licence is refused or queried, the company may submit additional site evidence within 10 business days or appeal to the Minister of Finance under s.11 of the Business Licence Act; pharmaceutical endorsement issues separately from the Department of Health once storage conditions are verified.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Health, Ministry of Health, Republic of Vanuatu (Pharmacy Unit / Vanuatu National Pharmacy Council), in coordination with the Business Licence Registrar (MFEM).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Pharmaceutical Wholesale and Import Business Licence (endorsed as API Wholesale / Distribution) issued under the Business Licence Act [Cap 218] and the Pharmacy Act [Cap 32].

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Justice and Community Services, Republic of Vanuatu.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Category C) – Exempt from a Full EIA Report. The undertaking is confined to warehousing, repackaging oversight, and wholesale distribution of APIs with no chemical synthesis or manufacturing; a Pharmaceutical Storage and Waste-Handling Registration Notice must be filed with DEPC.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater and no active VOC or particulate emission points are permitted; stormwater runoff from the warehouse must meet DEPC receiving-water quality standards; expired, recalled, or contaminated APIs must be classified as hazardous waste and handled only by DEPC-licensed waste contractors with a manifest-to-disposal record; wastewater from cleaning operations must not exceed pH 6–9 and chemical oxygen demand limits prescribed by the Vanuatu Pollution Control Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Vanuatu Fire and Emergency Services, including warehouse sprinkler adequacy and evacuation plan approval; structural load inspection certificate for the storage facility from the Public Works Department; occupational workplace health clearance under the Vanuatu Workplace Health and Safety regime, including chemical-agent employee exposure records, personal protective equipment programmes, and temperature-monitored pharmaceutical storage validation; local government physical-planning permit for warehouse use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Department of Customs and Inland Revenue (DCIR) — Government of the Republic of Vanuatu; official portal: https://customsinlandrevenue.gov.vu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act [Cap 222] via a private registered agent and register with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), lodging name reservation, memorandum and articles of association, registered office address in Port Vila, and registered agent details. Step 2: Obtain the VFSC Certificate of Incorporation. Step 3: Apply to the DCIR for the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) using the DCIR TIN application form, submitting certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, registered agent certificate, proof of registered office, and certified passport copies of directors/shareholders. Step 4: Where the IC makes or intends to make taxable supplies exceeding the VAT registration threshold, file Form VAT-001 (VAT Registration Application) with the DCIR, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, register of directors, service address, and a description of taxable activities. Step 5: Upon approval, the DCIR issues the VAT registration certificate and TIN, which must be quoted on all invoices and customs declarations. Step 6: For the wholesale distribution of pharmaceutical APIs, obtain the applicable trade/business licence and any VFSC endorsement required for the stated commercial model. The IC is tax-exempt by statute and is not obliged to pay income tax or business turnover taxes to the DCIR; voluntary TIN issuance is available for banking, customs clearance, and counterparty identity requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vanuatu maintains no check-the-box election, hybrid-mismatch election, or subchapter-S style classification regime. The International Company is automatically classified as an offshore tax-exempt entity under the International Companies Act [Cap 222], subject only to the statutory restriction that it must not carry on business with Vanuatu residents, hold land in Vanuatu, or list securities on the Vanuatu stock exchange. An IC may voluntarily deregister as an International Company and convert to a Domestic Company under the Companies Act, thereby subjecting itself to standard domestic tax treatment (including VAT and customs duties); this is a corporate-status conversion rather than a tax election. No other entity-level tax classification elections are available under Vanuatu law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 10,000,000 (ten million Vatu) annual taxable turnover; any person carrying on a taxable activity must register for VAT within 21 days after the end of the month in which the threshold is met, and may voluntarily register at a lower turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Vanuatu does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory API-based e-invoicing clearance, or digital tax-stamping platform. The DCIR accepts paper invoices, PDF e-invoices, and electronic records. Suppliers registered for VAT must issue a valid VAT invoice containing: the supplier's name and VAT registration number/TIN, sequential invoice number, date of issue, full description and quantity of goods or services, unit price and total consideration, the VAT amount at 15%, and for zero-rated exports an express statement that the supply is zero-rated under the Value Added Tax Act No. 13 of 2014. The DCIR is progressively digitising tax administration and customs declarations (including the electronic processing of export entries), but no statutory e-invoicing clearance mandate is in force as of the assessment date.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Section 13 of the Value Added Tax Act No. 13 of 2014 where the supplier exports the goods from Vanuatu within 28 days of the date of supply (or such further period as the Commissioner of Customs and Inland Revenue approves) and retains documentary evidence of export. Services are zero-rated where (a) the services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside Vanuatu at the time the services are performed; (b) the services are in respect of exported goods; or (c) the services relate to goods that are temporarily imported into Vanuatu for repair or processing and are subsequently exported. For the pharmaceutical API wholesale model, the IC must demonstrate that the APIs are physically dispatched to a foreign purchaser and leave Vanuatu, or are delivered from an offshore warehouse where the services are supplied for export-related logistics; commissionaire or bill-and-hold arrangements are scrutinised for substance. Relief from VAT on zero-rated exports is effected by crediting input tax against output tax; excess credits are refundable by the DCIR.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (approved export entry lodged with the DCIR Customs Division)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Vanuatu within 28 days of supply
Commercial Invoice and Packing List issued by the International Company to the overseas pharmaceutical buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT confirmation demonstrating settlement of the export proceeds in foreign currency
Certificate of Origin (where required by the destination jurisdiction or trade agreement)
Sales contract, Letter of Credit, or purchase order reflecting the offshore wholesale transaction
Customs entry or import documentation from the destination country confirming receipt of the APIs where available
Evidence of tax invoice issuance showing the zero-rated supply and VAT ID of the supplier
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DCIR conducts targeted audits of zero-rated export refunds, requiring a complete 'export evidence package' for each consignment; failure to produce satisfactory proof of physical export and foreign-currency consideration within the prescribed record-keeping period results in reversal of the zero-rating, assessment of VAT at the standard 15% rate on the full gross consideration, and imposition of interest at the statutory rate from the original due date. The Commissioner may issue default assessments where VAT returns are incorrect or where zero-rating is unsupported, and may raise assessments up to four years from the relevant date (extended in cases of fraudulent or wilful evasion). Penalties under the Value Added Tax Act No. 13 of 2014 include administrative fines of up to VT 1,000,000, additional penalties of up to 100% of the tax evaded, and imprisonment of up to three years for individuals involved in making false declarations or knowingly issuing fraudulent zero-rated invoices. The VFSC may additionally deregister or strike an International Company for non-compliance, and a breach of the IC Act's restriction on trading with Vanuatu residents will forfeit the IC's tax-exempt status, exposing the entity to retroactive domestic VAT and customs duty liabilities. Although Vanuatu imposes no statutory exchange-control repatriation timeline, standard banking compliance and the DCIR export-evidence framework effectively require repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days; documentation of later repatriation attracts enhanced scrutiny, potential denial of refund claims, and clawback of any VAT refund previously paid, together with penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) - Monetary Authority and Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu maintains a liberal exchange-control regime for both current and capital account transactions. The Vanuatu vatu (VUV) is freely convertible, profit remittances are not subject to prior exchange-control approval, and the International Company may repatriate paid-up capital and trading dividends without quantitative ceilings. Practical impediments arise only from bank-level AML/CFT due diligence, enhanced documentation for high-risk pharmaceutical wholesale activity, and RBV/FIU reporting thresholds for large-value or unusual inbound/outbound transfers. Sanctioned jurisdictions and persons remain prohibited under Vanuatu's international financial sanctions framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vanuatu imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline. Export receipts may be retained in a resident foreign-currency account, converted to VUV at licensed dealer rates, or used directly for import/trade settlements. A dealing bank will require the underlying pro-forma invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, insurance certificate, and customs export declaration for the trade to be processed under the liberalised regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low—Vanuatu has no statutory electronic-money institution (EMI) licensing category. Offshore digital banks and EMIs without an RBV banking licence cannot open resident VUV accounts, access the local clearing system, or provide regulated payment services to a Vanuatu International Company. They may be used only as supplementary payment gateways, not as primary treasury or settlement rails, and are legally constrained from issuing VUV-denominated accounts or executing local currency payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physically, the RBV's AML/CFT Guidelines require licensed banks to verify the identity of all directors and beneficial owners using reliable, independent documentation. In practice, the primary signatory director and the ultimate beneficial owner must attend an in-person interview at the bank's Port Vila branch before account mandates are activated for pharmaceutical API distribution. Remote video verification may be accepted for non-glass-tier secondary directors, but this remains at the sole discretion of the compliance officer; most tier-1 banks require at least one natural-person director with physical presence in Vanuatu.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived shell-company structure: non-resident International Company without demonstrable substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation; current Certificate of Good Standing from the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC); registered-office and licensed-agent agreements; signed lease or Virtual Office plus third-party logistics contracts; economic substance narrative demonstrating actual pharmaceutical API wholesale operations; audited financial statements or interim management accounts; corporate register extract listing directors and shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners unable to evidence lawful source of wealth and funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passports and address proof; bank reference letters from regulated financial institutions; source-of-wealth declaration supported by sale agreements, dividend vouchers, audited company accounts, or inheritance documents; 24-month original bank statements of the remitting party; negative PEP screening reports; sworn affidavit attesting to the legitimate origin of contributed capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pharmaceutical API transaction-chain integrity and anti-counterfeit exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid wholesale/import-export licences from the country of origin; supplier GMP certificates and manufacturing authorised-for-distribution letters; Certificate of Analysis (CoA) per product lot; temperature-controlled transport documentation and cold-chain logs; end-user/buyer compliance declarations; ESG/anti-bribery questionnaires; transaction-level inventory and shipping records retained for RBV/FIU inspection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must arrive via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's regulated overseas bank to the Vanuatu International Company's designated escrow/operational account at an RBV-licensed bank. The SWIFT field 70 (Remittance Information) must include an explicit corporate-purpose narrative, for example 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — VU_IC / ISIC 4649 / PHARMACEUTICAL API WHOLESALE', and must never be described as a personal gift or unrelated remittance. The receiving bank will require a board resolution authorising the incoming capital, a copy of the shareholder register, and a source-of-funds questionnaire for any transfer above the bank's threshold. Large-value inbound transfers may be subject to RBV/FIU high-value reporting; tranching artificial splits is prohibited and is itself an AML red flag.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements should use a dual-rail approach: for open-account and pre-payment trading, SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details, invoice reference, and ISIC 4649 trade description; for bulk API shipments, a commercial documentary Letter of Credit issued via a correspondent bank in the supplier jurisdiction, using SWIFT MT700/MT707 for issuance and amendments and SWIFT MT202/MT103 cover for reimbursement. The bank will require the underlying purchase order, supplier invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, packing list, and any import permits from the destination country before executing the payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivered FX forward contracts (USD/VUV, USD/EUR) with an RBV-licensed Vanuatu dealing bank
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on VUV executed through an approved overseas prime broker or bank, settling in USD offshore
FX swap contracts (spot vs forward) between USD, EUR, and VUV for trade cash-flow timing management
Cross-currency swap (USD/EUR) matching the IC's commercial invoicing and API procurement currencies
FX call/put options on the invoice currencies of the underlying pharmaceutical API trade, subject to bank suitability and enhanced transactional due diligence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Renewal Filing and Annual Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), International Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June; not aligned to the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts the VFSC-published late fee schedule; if outstanding fees remain unpaid for approximately three months, the International Company may be administratively struck off and lose legal capacity, affecting outstanding pharmaceutical contracts and banking arrangements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Agent Declaration and Confirmation of Members, Directors, and Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual renewal by 30 June; register updates for share transfers or director changes must be routed through the registered agent promptly after the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate filing fee; false or incomplete declarations and defective statutory registers constitute offences under the International Companies Act 2012, with penalties of up to VUV 400,000 (approximately USD 3,400) or 18 months' imprisonment, and may prevent issuance of certificates of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit and Verification of On-Site Statutory Records by the Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent acting under VFSC supervisory expectations; corrective filing only where discrepancies are identified
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed annually no later than 30 June and upon any change of registered agent or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficiencies must be remedied within VFSC-prescribed timeframes; persistent non-compliance may lead to monetary penalties, administrative strike-off, or refusal of a certificate of good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to a Vanuatu International Company in the tax-exempt regime. An audit or financial review may be required only if mandated by the company's articles, shareholder resolution, lender agreement, or VFSC direction.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act 2012 (as amended); no mandatory statutory presentation framework is imposed on tax-exempt International Companies. If financial statements are voluntarily prepared, International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or IFRS for SMEs are the customary framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At annual renewal, the registered agent obtains a written confirmation from the directors identifying all ultimate beneficial owners. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be promptly recorded in the beneficial ownership register and incorporated into the agent's annual declaration. Vanuatu does not require a public UBO filing for International Companies, but the register must remain available for lawful inspection by the VFSC and the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 950 – USD 1,800 per annum for a licensed Vanuatu registered agent and registered office, including AML and compliance coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 7,000 per voluntary audit or agreed-upon-procedures engagement prepared on an IFRS basis

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Company (IC) enjoys a full, automatic exemption from Vanuatu income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty under Section 41 of the International Companies Act Cap 222. No corporate income tax return, no estimation, and no payment is required. The only annual exaction is the VFSC annual registration fee (approximately VUV 30,000-50,000, depending on the registered agent's tariff).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No CIT return is issued or accepted by the Vanuatu Revenue and Customs Authority (VRCA). Compliance is performed through the VFSC annual return and fee, submitted electronically by the licensed registered agent via the VFSC online registry portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The VFSC annual fee and declaration must be settled no later than the anniversary date of incorporation each year. There is no statutory corporate income tax filing deadline because no income tax filing obligation exists for an IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered name of the International Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name on the VFSC Certificate of Incorporation. No deviation is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, and licence number of the VFSC-licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent must be physically resident in Vanuatu. Non-resident directors or beneficial owners cannot act as registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical street address of the registered office in Port Vila.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A real office address in Vanuatu is mandatory. Post office boxes are not acceptable; the registered agent's address may be used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the IC is exempt from Vanuatu income tax on all foreign-source income and on any income derived from the licensed exempt activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To preserve the exemption, the IC should not derive income from Vanuatu domestic trading and must not hold Vanuatu real estate. No tax election is required for non-resident owners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No CIT late-filing penalty applies as no CIT return exists. Failure to pay the VFSC annual fee by the anniversary date triggers a 10% late penalty surcharge; continued default (typically beyond 90 days) exposes the IC to automatic strike-off and dissolution under Part IX of the International Companies Act Cap 222. The registered agent may also be fined for non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Vanuatu imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by an International Company to any shareholder, whether resident or non-resident.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has no comprehensive double taxation agreement (DTA) network in force. No treaty claim, no tax residency certificate, and no TRC filing procedure is available or necessary because the exemption is direct and automatic under Section 41 of the International Companies Act Cap 222. For banking and counterparty purposes, the IC may obtain a Certificate of Good Standing and an ad-hoc Certificate of Tax Exemption Status from the VFSC, issued through the registered agent, confirming zero Vanuatu tax liability.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties and debt interest is 0%. Vanuatu also does not levy any branch remittance tax, management fee withholding, or notional interest deduction restrictions. No treaty rate applies because no DTA exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Vanuatu has no transfer pricing legislation and no statutory VUV threshold for Local File or Master File preparation. Best-practice threshold: if the foreign parent group is subject to OECD-style TP rules, prepare a balanced Local File for the Vanuatu IC when annual related-party turnover exceeds VUV 120 million (approx. USD 1 million) or when intercompany financial transactions exceed VUV 50 million (approx. USD 400,000), aligning with common EU/OECD de-minimis rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu introduced economic substance requirements via the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2022 and the VFSC Economic Substance Guidance, applicable to 'relevant activities' including distribution and service centres, financing and leasing, headquarters, holding entities, and IP businesses. A pharmaceutical API wholesale IC holding a VFSC special-purpose licence and engaging in related-party distribution must demonstrate in Vanuatu: (i) local board meetings with quorum; (ii) adequate physical premises and equipment; (iii) a minimum of one full-time resident employee; (iv) substantive decision-making at principal level; and (v) annual operating expenditure proportionate to the income booked. An annual economic substance notification must be filed with the VFSC; failure to file or to satisfy substance triggers monetary penalties, loss of licence, and possible deregistration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Tax Exemption / Foreign Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Vanuatu IC as a bare booking vehicle while the true place of effective management remains in the foreign parent's high-tax jurisdiction; executing back-to-back API sale and purchase contracts without any Vanuatu personnel; failing to disclose the IC's role in the foreign group's tax filings; artificially inflating the IC's profit margin to shift taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Within Vanuatu, no domestic income tax fraud charge arises because the IC is exempt; however, knowingly making false statements to VFSC constitutes an offence under the International Companies Act Cap 222, attracting a fine of up to VUV 500,000. Outside Vanuatu, the parent jurisdiction may apply CFC rules, GAAR, or transfer pricing recharacterisation, resulting in retroactive tax assessments, interest, and penalties of 100%-200% of the tax underpaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false intercompany agreements or knowingly misstate the IC's management location face personal criminal liability in Vanuatu, including a fine and imprisonment of up to 2 years. In the foreign jurisdiction, directors can be personally assessed for the diverted tax, subjected to travel bans, and disqualified from serving as directors under cross-border enforcement mechanisms.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC to receive or transmit proceeds derived from counterfeit pharmaceutical sales or narcotics trafficking; accepting API payments from unknown ultimate beneficial owners; layering funds through multiple shell entities; executing Swift LC or bank-wire transactions without adequate source-of-wealth and KYC documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act, Act No. 7 of 2016, a corporate body convicted of money laundering faces fines of up to VUV 20 million, mandatory revocation of the VFSC licence, and confiscation of all connected assets. The Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) may freeze bank accounts and order the surrender of transaction records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and authorised signatories who knowingly or recklessly participate in laundering API proceeds are liable to imprisonment of up to 15 years, individual fines of up to VUV 5 million, travel bans, and asset seizure under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2001.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients under ISIC 4649 without a valid Vanuatu pharmaceutical import/export licence; distributing APIs that are not registered or that fail WHO prequalification standards; falsifying batch certificates, certificates of analysis, or customs declarations for controlled precursor chemicals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Contravention of the Pharmacy Act Cap 65 and related medicines regulations subjects the company to immediate product seizure, revocation of any distribution authorisation, and fines of up to VUV 10 million per offence; each API shipment or falsified document constitutes a separate offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise the import/export of counterfeit or unregistered APIs are personally and criminally liable, facing fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years, permanent exclusion from acting as a director of any licensed pharmaceutical company, and civil claims by downstream patients or distributors for damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Substance Failure and Sanctions Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming the 'distribution and service centre' relevant activity in the annual substance notification without employing any local staff or using any local premises; continuing to trade after the VFSC licence has lapsed; routing API shipments to entities located in OFAC/EU/UN sanctioned jurisdictions using disguised invoice intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VFSC may impose an initial fine of up to VUV 500,000 and a continuing penalty of VUV 50,000 per month for non-compliance, suspend the registered agent's services, and strike off the IC. Sanctions violations are referred to the Vanuatu FIU and the Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Unit, which can execute restraint orders on the IC's bank accounts and compel repatriation of misappropriated assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for false substance declarations and sanctions evasion, including fines of up to VUV 1,000,000, imprisonment of up to 10 years, director disqualification orders, travel bans, and personal confiscation of profits earned through the offending transactions.
